scene_description: Topic ideation for class presentations, thesis defenses, work reports, business pitches and conference talks. Produces topics that can be covered within the time and slide limits, with a clear presentation purpose.

questions.question: What is the occasion for this presentation?
What is the subject area of the presentation? (course / project / business area)
How do you want to support the presentation?
Which content must be included? (e.g. a project's data, a theoretical framework, a product demo)
What minefields or content do you want to avoid?

skip_logic.description: Adjust the questions and topic scope based on occasion and length.
rules: If the user picks "thesis defense", skip the humor question, treat the tone as academic, and ensure the topic can answer committee questions about novelty
If the user picks "business pitch" with a "clients or investors" audience, ask about the product and data status, and add a "commercialization and key metrics" field to the output
If the user picks "under 5 minutes", suggest no more than 10 slides and keep a single core point; no multi-topic mashups
If the user picks "data and charts", ask about data sources in Step 3; with no existing data, suggest argument- or narrative-led topics instead and note the data gap in the risk warnings
If the user picks "visual and image-led", add visual presentation suggestions and warn against text-heavy slides

tone_examples: Good: Quarterly user retention rose 4 points quarter over quarter, mainly from two changes to the onboarding flow.
Good: Over the next three slides, we explain why we picked this direction, how we will do it, and what resources we need.
Bad: Hi everyone, here with another filler report, let me just wing it.
Bad: This project is huge, just trust me, you cannot go wrong.
conditional_notes: For "thesis defense" or academic conferences, switch to an academic tone and no colloquial expressions.
For "class presentation" where the user picks "jokes and interaction welcome", mild humor in the opening and cases is fine, but the conclusion must be complete.

constraint_list: The topic must be coverable within the allotted time, and the slide count must match the duration
Each slide carries one core point, and the whole talk has one clear main line
There must be a clear purpose: inform, persuade, show, or recommend a decision
The depth must match the audience's knowledge level
Key conclusions must be backed by data, facts or literature; no empty talk
The topic must cover the content required in must_include
exclusion_rules: Big themes that cannot be covered within the slide / time limits
Jargon and unexplained abbreviations the audience cannot follow
Assertions with no factual backing, especially in defense and business settings
Warm-up and personal asides unrelated to the occasion
Segments needing complex demo conditions that the venue cannot guarantee
Content the user explicitly lists in excludes
